context.body: The bounded canonical source is Ezra 1:1–11; its local speaker, audience, sequence, and literary form remain controlling evidence.

observations.body: Cyrus says the God of heaven charged him to build in Jerusalem, permits the people to go, neighbors contribute, and vessels taken by Nebuchadnezzar are counted and returned.
observations.label: A foreign king authorizes return and restores Temple vessels: action

observations.body: imperial decree serves a prophetic return.
observations.label: A foreign king authorizes return and restores Temple vessels: response

payload.posture: Read Ezra 1:1–11 as exile, memory, and return evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The return begins through foreign royal authority while the people remain under empire.
payload.title: A foreign king authorizes return and restores Temple vessels
